title: Hess Highway: ΔH via Cycles
welcome_lead: Apply Hess's law to compute unmeasurable enthalpy changes.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on Hess cycle calculations.
final_note: You navigated alternate routes to the same ΔH.

concepts.def: ΔH depends only on start and end.

walkthroughs.body_html:
For aA + bB -> cC + dD: ΔHr = (c×ΔHf C + d×ΔHf D) - (a×ΔHf A + b×ΔHf B).

Set ΔHf of elements in standard states to zero.

ΔHr = Σ ΔHc(reactants) - Σ ΔHc(products). Apply when ΔHc data is given.

Useful for forming hydrocarbons from elements where direct route is impractical.

mcqs.q: When you reverse a reaction in a Hess cycle, what happens to ΔH?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
Its sign reverses — if the forward reaction is +100 kJ/mol, the reverse is -100 kJ/mol.
ΔH stays the same because it's the same reaction.
Hess's Law works because energy always cancels out around any cycle.
Hess's Law works because reactions can only happen in one specific direction.
Enthalpy is a state function — change depends only on initial and final states, not the route taken.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
